meta.problem: Understand founders' pain points and discover what they want to use their agent for, the way solution architects, developer relations and sales engineers run discovery calls, with a Chief of Staff that deploys specialised agents.

agents.name: chief-of-staff
agents.system_summary: Dispatches one discovery call per founder persona plus the Linear and Notion scouts in parallel threads, then hands every evidence item to the miner and merges the result into the room report.

agents.name: discovery-agent
agents.system_summary: Runs a solution-engineer-style discovery call (6-8 questions, past behaviour over hypotheticals) and writes a needs brief.
agents.output: needs brief: use_case, current_workaround, blockers (with verbatim quotes), definition_of_done, cma_mapping

agents.name: founder-priya / founder-tomas / founder-aisha / founder-ben
agents.system_summary: One agent per persona; persona lives in `system`, generated by agents/make_founders.py.

agents.name: linear-scout
agents.system_summary: v0: reads the seeded Linear export mounted at /mnt/session/uploads/linear/tickets.json (mock connector). v1: hosted Linear MCP (agents/linear-scout.mcp-v1.json.example).

agents.name: notion-scout
agents.system_summary: v0: reads the seeded Notion page export mounted at /mnt/session/uploads/notion/ (mock connector) and normalises relevant blocks into evidence items. v1: same behaviour via the Notion API.

agents.name: miner
agents.system_summary: Clusters pain points across all transcripts and briefs, keeps verbatim quotes, ranks fixes, and tallies blockers by CMA primitive.

agents.name: data-analyst
agents.system_summary: After the miner: inventories data, builds SQLite tables (stdlib only), computes metrics.json, writes a self-contained inline-SVG dashboard.html.

agents.name: retro
agents.system_summary: Separate session after each run: reads run-journal (read_only), writes method-only lessons to the three lessons stores (read_write). No Linear/Notion access.

audience.deliverable: Top pains founders hit building managed agents, each with quotes and the doc, skill or API fix

outcome.description: Run discovery with every founder persona, collect Slack and Notion evidence, and produce room-report.md plus one needs brief per founder in /mnt/session/outputs/
rubric_criteria: room-report.md ranks at least 5 pain clusters by number of distinct founders mentioning each
Every cluster has at least 2 verbatim quotes, each tagged with its source (call, linear or notion) and a link or transcript reference
Every quote appears word for word in the collected evidence; no paraphrase is presented as a quote
Evidence from all three sources (call, linear, notion) appears in the report
Every founder has a needs brief with all 5 fields (use_case, current_workaround, blockers, definition_of_done, cma_mapping), and cma_mapping uses real CMA primitive names
Every cluster ends with one concrete fix (doc, skill or API change), and the report includes a blocker tally by CMA primitive
run-manifest.json has a done entry with existing outputs for every numbered kickoff step; dashboard.html and data/metrics.json exist and every dashboard number appears in metrics.json
outcome.answer_key: evals/<case>/answer-key.json holds each case's hidden pains. It is never mounted into the session or placed in the rubric; recall is graded outside the run.

stores.name: pain-library
stores.purpose: Cumulative pain clusters with counts and first/last seen, so each digest leads with new and growing clusters

stores.name: discovery-lessons
stores.purpose: Method lessons: which question patterns surfaced pains, which fell flat

stores.name: scout-lessons
stores.purpose: Source quirks and what counted as relevant evidence

stores.name: coordinator-playbook
stores.purpose: Dispatch and merge lessons, plus the retro log of each run's verdicts

stores.name: run-journal
stores.purpose: What each sweep did, self-assessed gaps and grader feedback; input for the retro (read_only there)

deployments.name: room-sweep
deployments.what: Linear and Notion scouts collect evidence since the last run, miner updates pain-library, digest of new and growing clusters. No simulated founders.

deployments.name: room-retro
deployments.what: Retro session: reads the latest sweep's transcript and verdict, writes method lessons (lessons stores read_write, no Linear/Notion access).

schedule.kickoff: user.define_outcome, relative dates only ('since the last run', 'as of this run')

cases.name: case-01
cases.input: 4 simulated discovery calls + seeded Linear tickets + 1 seeded Notion page (~12 hidden pains)

cases.name: case-02
cases.authors: Founder writes 1-2 personas (template: evals/case-02/personas/TEMPLATE.md), Claude writes the rest; breaks circularity with the discovery playbook.

evals.pass_bar: recall >= 80% of answer-key pains and 0 fabricated quotes
evals.notes: Two-layer grading: Outcome rubric checks structure and faithfulness in-run; evals check recall against the answer key after the run.
evals.learning_claim: Recall rising on case-01 alone is not evidence of learning; only claim improvement when case-02 (never seen by retro) holds or improves.

layers.outcome: In-run: the 7 rubric criteria incl. the run manifest (did the task, everything asked done).
layers.trace: Post-run: evals/trace_eval.py over session events and threads (made the right calls: one discovery thread per founder, both scouts dispatched, miner then data-analyst after scouts, <=8 questions per call, verbatim relay, no unexpected calls; manifest cross-checked against the trace).
layers.recall: Post-run: evals/score.py against answer-key.json (achieved the goal: recall >= 0.8, 0 fabricated quotes).

scoreboard.why: Decide whether the token cost per task is worth it, and compare agent versions and effort settings.

mocked.how: evals/case-01/linear/tickets.json mounted via Files API; v1 payload ready in agents/linear-scout.mcp-v1.json.example

connections.notes: v0 has no external credentials. Founder chose to mock Linear instead of creating a personal API key; the Claude Code Linear connector (after re-auth) is used only to seed the real demo team for v1.

model_rationale: Opus everywhere: quality first for discovery, clustering and orchestration.

learning_loop.fast_loop: Every run: Outcome grade-and-revise (max_iterations 3). Then a separate retro session (chief-of-staff) reads the run's transcript, Outcome verdict and eval results, and writes evidence-cited method lessons to the lessons stores; the next run reads them first.
learning_loop.slow_loop: Agent/skill changes ship as new agent versions, promoted to the deployment only after evals (case-01 + held-back case-02) hold.
guards: Main run mounts the three lessons stores read_only; only the retro session mounts them read_write (enforced by the API, since memory mounts are per session and shared by all threads)
Slack/Notion content is untrusted input: it never runs in a session that can write lessons
Lessons are about method, never content (no pain names or answers)
Eval runs mount every store read_only so held-back cases cannot be memorised
Lessons cite the run and evidence that produced them; memory versions give a 30-day audit trail
learning_loop.retro_mode: auto-write, audited via memory versions and evals

digest_dedup: pain-library memory store: digest leads with new and growing clusters, then a one-line unchanged list

live_mode.what: A judge plays founder #5 live: a single-agent session on discovery-agent, answered by a human in their own terminal via `ant beta:sessions connect`; the resulting transcript + brief are added to the room report.
live_mode.why: Proves discovery works on a real human, not only simulated personas.

design_notes: Simulated founders are separate agents with the persona in `system`, never files, so no other agent can read hidden pains via the shared filesystem.
discovery-agent has only the `write` tool enabled.
Only the coordinator can message sub-agents (send_to_agent); it relays questions and answers verbatim.
Sweep writes a run-journal memory store; retro reads it read_only and writes method lessons.

telemetry.what: Per run: model slug, effort per agent, input/output/cache tokens, cost split (input vs output vs cache vs runtime) from pricing.json, API list_cost total, peak context per thread where the event stream exposes it, active seconds.
telemetry.where: launch.sh `card` step prints it; the overview run-log row gets the same numbers.
